blindSummary:
A major city here and the adjoining former-foreign-military-basing corridor constitute this state/province's principal traveller-facing risk. In June 2025 the district office of a national investigation agency dismantled a trafficking ring at a bar in that city, arresting four people and rescuing 45 victims including 13 minors; in March 2025 the same office arrested a foreign national and accomplices under the national anti-trafficking law, rescuing 12 more victims. Peer-reviewed research describes the foreign military-basing economy around the corridor as sustaining sexual markets that "disproportionately exploit poor transgender women," and a 2024 external anti-trafficking report confirms traffickers exploit victims in tourist destinations and urban areas.

For a transgender visitor the exposure is two-fold: the environments where trans women are concentrated in sex work carry the highest violence and trafficking risk, and enforcement sweeps can sweep up anyone in the vicinity. There is no protective ordinance cluster here comparable to the national capital district or other leading states/provinces.

Net effect: a clear negative deviation from the national baseline. The trafficking-exposure pattern is structural and documented rather than a single incident. Compare a neighbouring state/province, which has one killing but no comparable commercial-sex-economy infrastructure drawing visitors into maximum-exposure environments.
